issues.issue: The confidentiality bar is absolute on its face ("ANY REPRODUCTION OR DISTRIBUTION ... IS PROHIBITED") with no carve-out, and the phrase "BY ACCEPTING THIS MEMORANDUM" leaves the moment of assent undefined. Neither point names a term of real commercial bite.

The flat prohibition here is qualified by the later CONFIDENTIAL/TRADE SECRET paragraph, which permits distribution to the recipient's own financial and legal advisors; the two consent regimes are not expressly reconciled.

The instruction that investors "MUST RELY ON THEIR OWN EXAMINATION" sits against the Executive Summary's affirmative representations about targeted returns and past performance, but the Memorandum expressly qualifies those elsewhere.

Transfers are permitted only "AS PROVIDED IN THE NOTE PURCHASE AGREEMENT", while the Summary of Principal Terms "Transfers of Notes" allows certain family-trust, affiliate and operation-of-law transfers without consent; the relationship between the two statements is not spelled out.
"WITHOUT UNREASONABLE EFFORT OR EXPENSE" is an undefined standard limiting the promise to supply additional information, with no benchmark supplied.

The reserved "RIGHT TO MODIFY ANY OF THE TERMS OF THE OFFERING AND THE OFFERING DOCUMENTS" is difficult to square with the Summary of Principal Terms "Amendments, Waivers of Noteholder Agreements", which requires approval of a Majority in Interest of Noteholders for any modification of the Note Purchase Agreement, Notes or Security Agreement.

The recipient is made to "agree" that the contents "ARE A TRADE SECRET" and are subject to "REASONABLE EFFORTS TO MAINTAIN THEIR SECRECY", an undefined standard imported from statute and applied to an entire document of mixed public and private content.

"[T]argeting to return approximately 8.00% or more per year" and "superior returns with a conservative risk profile" are aspirational and unmeasurable, yet appear alongside the flat statement that the Notes "will be secured by the assets of the Company".

The unqualified promise that the Notes "will be secured by the assets of the Company" is in tension with the "Company Borrowings" term and the "Use of capital and Company borrowings" paragraph, which permit senior liens on those same assets ahead of the Noteholders.

The stated purpose is confined to financing "commercial real estate or for other real estate related purposes", whereas Section IV permits residential construction loans and loans collateralized by other loans; the catch-all "other real estate related purposes" must do the reconciling work.

This paragraph says the initial closing is expected "on or before December 3, 2007" with monthly closings "through May 1, 2009", while the Summary of Principal Terms "Closing" fixes the initial closing at December 1, 2007 and the final closing at the end of the sixth full quarter (estimated June 30, 2009).
"[S]ubject to a minimum average rate of eight percent (8%) annualized" is ambiguous as to whether 8% is a floor on each quarterly rate or only on an average computed over some unstated period.

The "minimum average rate" formulation conflicts with the Note Terms and Payment provision, which states flatly that "[t]he Floating Rate will not be less than 8% on an annualized basis for a calendar year".

The one-year bar on requesting prepayment is stated without the further conditions imposed by the "Return of Investment; Early Payment of Note" term (sixty days' notice and an effective date on the last business day of a fiscal quarter), so the two descriptions of the same right differ.

The statement that Noteholders "will be secured creditors of the Company" cannot be squared without qualification with the "Failure of Security" risk factor and the "Company Borrowings" term, which contemplate that the Noteholders' interest may be subordinated and may not even be perfected.

The permission to raise Note proceeds to pay expenses and compensation, and to grant liens senior to the Notes, is in tension with the Executive Summary's statement that "[t]he Notes will be secured by the assets of the Company" and with the description of Noteholders as secured creditors.
"[C]onservatively underwritten", "sub-prime mortgage market" and "quality real estate" are undefined qualitative standards whose boundaries could not be applied without extrinsic evidence.

The undertaking that the Company "will not source loans for the purpose of resale" is in tension with "Sale of Loans Generally", which permits occasional sales of mortgage loans and sales of non-performing loans to affiliates.

The claim that "no investor has experienced a loss of investment principal" is a promotional recital that sits against the operative risk factors warning of possible total loss, but the paragraph itself disclaims any assurance of similar results.

The assertion of a "100% collection record" and that no predecessor fund "experienced a loss of principal or interest" is a promotional recital pointing in a different direction from the operative Risk Factors section and the "no operating history" disclaimer that immediately follows.

This disclaimer that projections are "FOR ILLUSTRATION PURPOSES ONLY" is difficult to reconcile with the Executive Summary's affirmative statement that the Company targets a return of "approximately 8.00% or more per year".

The statement that the Servicer "will originate or arrange all loans acquired by the Company" conflicts with the "Right to retain other firms" paragraph and with "Purchase of Loans from Servicer", which permit the Company to buy loans from unrelated third parties and to retain other firms in lieu of the Servicer.

The Manager's reserved right to "terminate all or any portion of their business relationship with the Company at any time" is difficult to reconcile with the "Restricted Actions" term, which forbids the Manager to "[w]ithdraw as the sole manager of the Company" without the approval of a Majority in Interest of Noteholders.

The routing of compensation between Company, Manager and Servicer here is restated in different terms under "Servicer Compensation, Compensation from Portfolio Borrowers", which directs fees to the Manager where the Manager contracts with or itself performs Loan Services; the two descriptions overlap imperfectly.

The disclaimer that the Manager owes no fiduciary duty is in tension with the repeated statements elsewhere that "Noteholders must rely on the good faith and integrity of the Manager" and with the Delaware fiduciary duty the same paragraph acknowledges.

The exculpation/indemnity standard stated here ("fraud, bad faith or willful misconduct") differs from the standard in the Summary of Principal Terms "Exculpation and Indemnification" term, which conditions indemnity on the absence of "willful misconduct or gross negligence".

The direction that Noteholders "must rely on the good faith and integrity of the Manager" cannot easily be squared with the immediately preceding disclaimer that the Manager owes the Noteholders no fiduciary obligation.

The cross-reference is to "Fiduciary Responsibility of the Managing Member", a heading that does not exist in this Memorandum, which instead carries "No Fiduciary Responsibility of Manager to Noteholders".

"[T]he rate generally prevailing in the geographical areas where the security property is located for loans to comparable borrowers of similar size, duration and security" is a standard with no defined reference point, and "generally" leaves it non-binding.
The Manager's right to retain other firms "in lieu of the Servicer" is in tension with the statement that "[t]he Servicer will originate or arrange all loans acquired by the Company".

"Related Party Loans" is defined by an open-ended illustration ("such as a loan under which the borrower is owned by one or more of the members ... or their family members"), leaving the outer reach of affiliation uncertain.

This limit binds "at any time" against "total Company assets at such time", whereas the parallel "Loans to Related Parties" statement in Section IV tests the same 20% cap only "upon the closing of the Related Party Loan in question"; the two tests give different answers as assets change.

"[C]onsistent with the lending standards and policies set forth above" is vague as to which standards are incorporated, and "loan terms typically offered by the Company on similar loans" has no benchmark for a company with no operating history.
"[A]ny material event of default" leaves the materiality threshold and what counts as an "event of default" for these purposes undefined.

The mandatory purchase trigger here (a "material event of default" continuing 90 consecutive days) differs from the Section IV "Loans to Related Parties" restatement, which requires purchase whenever "the Loan is in default more than 90 days" without any materiality qualifier.

The defined term is introduced as "Other Sponsored Investment Funds" but the same paragraph and later provisions also use "Other Sponsored Funds" and "Sponsored Investment Funds" without defining them, leaving the allocation covenant's scope uncertain.
The exhortation that Noteholders "must rely on the Manager to act in good faith" is in tension with the express disclaimer of any fiduciary obligation of the Manager to Noteholders.
"[O]nly so much time to the business of the Company as is reasonably required" sets no measurable commitment of management time.
"[T]he Manager's first priority will usually be" states no obligation at all, and "so much thereof as can reasonably be obtained in light of current market conditions" is an unmeasurable standard.

The pricing formula says the price shall be "not less than any of the following" and then lists three alternatives joined by "or"; read literally "not less than any" means not less than the lowest, while the list structure suggests the highest of the three must be met.

The statement that affiliate seller financing "will not be deemed a Related Party Loan" removes such loans from the 20% cap and mandatory-repurchase rules in the "Loans to Related Parties" provisions, an exclusion those provisions do not themselves acknowledge.
The paragraph is garbled — "expects to purchase mortgage loans from, or later into co-investment agreements with, R.E. Loans" omits a verb ("enter"), obscuring what the Company commits to do.

It refers to compliance with criteria for "Sponsored Investment Funds or Private Clients", terms not defined anywhere in the Memorandum, which elsewhere defines only "Other Sponsored Investment Funds".
"[L]ocated primarily in the United States" gives no measurable limit, and "occasional loans" collateralized by other loans is similarly unbounded.

The permission to lend on "real estate located primarily in the United States" is quantified elsewhere by "Geographic Area of Lending Activity", which caps non-U.S. lending at 20% of total Company Capital; the two formulations of the same limit differ.

The loan-to-value table gives only two categories, "Improved Property" and "Land", with no ratio for loans that fall in neither (e.g., loans collateralized by other loans or partially improved land), and "Land" is left undefined.

The guidelines are described as "a strict set of guidelines" that the Company "expects to select loans" under, while the "Loan-to-Value Ratios" paragraph immediately following says the percentages "generally will not exceed" and the following paragraph exempts whole categories of loans.

The 20% cap is measured against "the Company's entire Loan Portfolio", a phrase used nowhere else and not defined, whereas the parallel caps in this section are measured against "total Company assets" and "total Company Capital".
"[P]rimarily" and the undefined measure "total Company Capital" leave the geographic limit without a workable boundary.

The 20% non-U.S. allowance is hard to square with the Summary of Principal Terms "Purpose", which describes the Company's purpose as loans on real property "located primarily in the United States" without any offshore allowance.

Valuation may be "as determined by either the Manager or an independent written appraisal", which permits the loan-to-value test to be satisfied on the Manager's own unreviewed valuation, and "generally will not exceed" makes the ratio non-binding.
The words "generally will not exceed" undercut the preceding description of the ratios as "a strict set of guidelines" designed to set standards for security quality.

"[A]ny reasonable financing terms that it deems to be in the best interests of the Company, in its sole discretion" combines an objective standard (reasonable) with an unreviewable subjective one (sole discretion).

The carve-out that affiliate purchase-money financing "shall [not] constitute a Related Party Loan" removes such transactions from the Related Party Loan caps and repurchase obligation set out in Section III.

Loans of up to six years may be made under this provision even though the Notes mature December 31, 2014 and the Company's term ends two years after that, so late-made long loans could outlast the funding they secure.

Permitting loans to borrowers already in default or without qualifying income is difficult to reconcile with the Section II undertaking that the Company will invest in "conservatively underwritten" loans and "will not operate in the sub-prime mortgage market".
"Satisfactory title insurance coverage" does not say satisfactory to whom or by what measure, though the balance of the sentence supplies the amount and named insured.
"Satisfactory fire and casualty insurance" is unmeasured, and the cross-reference is to a "Risk Factors – Uninsured Losses" heading that does not appear in the Memorandum.

This item is listed as one of the escrow "conditions" that must be "met" before disbursement, but it states only that the Manager does not intend to arrange mortgage insurance — it is not a condition at all.
As drafted it contradicts the introductory sentence of "Escrow Conditions", which says the escrow agent will not disburse "until the following conditions are met"; item (c) cannot be met.

The undertaking that "Company investments in Loans will not be held in the name of the Manager or any other nominee" is in tension with the permission in "General Standards for Mortgage Loans" to invest indirectly through an entity formed to hold a qualifying loan.

This restatement tests the 20% Related Party Loan cap only "upon the closing of the Related Party Loan in question" and requires repurchase whenever the loan is "in default more than 90 days", whereas Section III's standards test the cap "at any time" and require a "material event of default" continuing 90 consecutive days.

The general rule that the price "will not exceed the par value of the note or its fair market value, whichever is lower" is qualified by "[g]enerally" and by a premium exception resting on the Manager's own belief that the price "is fair and reasonable".

The premium exception is available only for purchases "from unaffiliated parties", yet the same paragraph says the Company will buy most or all loans from the affiliated Servicer; the pricing rule for affiliate purchases is left to the Note Purchase Agreement.

The text is garbled — "to achieve comparable with Sponsored Investment Funds" is missing a noun and "purchase from, sale to, of a co-investment with" should read "or" — obscuring the scope of the covenant.

The provision uses "Sponsored Investment Funds" and "Private Clients" as if defined, but the Memorandum defines only "Other Sponsored Investment Funds" in Section III, leaving the class of counterparties governed by these criteria uncertain.

The permitted dealings with Noteholders are made subject to "the criteria established by the Note Purchase Agreement for such affiliated transactions", criteria never stated in this Memorandum and referred to inconsistently across Sections III and IV.

The 20% diversification cap applies only "[a]fter the second year of the Company's term" and is measured against "the capital of the Company", a measure undefined and different from the "total Company assets" used for the Related Party Loan cap.

The reserve fund "may be funded by the Manager from any source, including capital raised from the sale of Notes", which sits against the Executive Summary's description of Note proceeds as capital raised for Portfolio Loans and expenses.

Sales of non-performing loans and foreclosed property to affiliates are permitted here without repeating the pricing floor imposed by "Sale of Defaulted Loans or Real Estate Owned to Affiliates" in Section III.
The permission to "occasionally sell mortgage loans" is in tension with the Section II undertaking that the Company "will not source loans for the purpose of resale".

The cross-reference is to "Risks and Other Important Factors - Risks of Leverage", a heading that does not exist in the Memorandum, whose risk section is titled "VII. Risk Factors" and contains no such subheading.

This provision says subscriptions are accepted "in the discretion of the Managing Member", a role the Memorandum never defines and which is elsewhere given to the Manager (see "Noteholders" in the Summary of Principal Terms).
"[S]uch other directly related activities ... as the Manager deems reasonably necessary or appropriate" is a general catch-all following specific enumerated activities, leaving its reach uncertain.

The statement that "[t]he Company may admit additional or substitute managers" is not reconciled with the "Restricted Actions" term barring the Manager from withdrawing as sole manager without a Majority in Interest, nor with the definition of the Manager as The Mortgage Fund LLC.

The Manager's power to delegate to "one or more qualified servicing entities" is stated without the qualification, appearing in Section III, that the Manager may retain other firms "in lieu of" the Servicer and that the Servicer will originate all Company loans.

"A minimum investment is 20,000 Units, in the discretion of the Manager" is self-contradictory as written: it states a minimum and then makes the minimum discretionary, without saying who may waive it or on what terms.

Eligibility is stated by reference to "accredited investors" under the Securities Act, whereas Section VIII "Suitable Investors" sets out its own enumerated categories and dollar thresholds; the two eligibility statements are not expressly harmonised.
